observations.question: I changed phones and Authenticator is blocking my login.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re being locked out after switching phones – let’s get your authenticator set up again so you can log in.

**Steps to re‑register Microsoft Authenticator on your new phone**

1. **Go to the Amref login page** and enter your AmIU email address (username) and password as you normally would.  
2. When the sign‑in process prompts for additional verification, choose the option to **set up the Microsoft Authenticator app** (if you see a link that says “I want to set up a different method”, you can ignore it for now and pick the authenticator app).  
3. **Download the Microsoft Authenticator app** on your new phone from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.  
4. Open the app on your phone and **scan the QR code** shown on the login screen.  
5. After the QR code is scanned, click **Next** on the computer/browser screen.  
6. Enter your **country code and phone number**, then click **Next**.  
7. You will receive a **code from Microsoft** on your mobile phone; enter that code and click **Next**.  
8. Click **Next** through any remaining prompts until you see the confirmation message that the setup is complete.  

Once these steps are finished, the next time you sign in you’ll be able to approve the login request from the Microsoft Authenticator app on your new phone.

**Note** – If you prefer to use SMS instead of the authenticator app, you can select **“I want to set up a different method”** at step 2, enter your mobile number, and verify the 6‑digit code sent by text message (see the tip in article 10 that recommends the authenticator app for a faster, more secure experience).

**Sources**  
- Setting up Microsoft Authenticator – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=11  
- Set up your Microsoft 365 sign‑in for multi‑factor authentication – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=10

observations.question: How can I enroll for 2FA on Office 365?
observations.answer:
I’ll walk you through enabling two‑factor authentication (2FA) for your Office 365/Microsoft 365 account using the steps documented in the Amref Help Desk Knowledge Base.

**Steps to enroll for 2FA on Office 365**

1. **Sign in to Microsoft 365**  
   Go to the Microsoft 365 sign‑in page and enter your work or school email address and password, then click **Sign in**. After you submit your password, you will be prompted for more information (see the dialog box shown below).

2. **Click Next**  
   On the prompt that asks for additional verification, select the **Next** button.

3. **Choose your verification method**  
   The default option is the **Microsoft Authenticator** app.  
   - If you already have the Microsoft Authenticator app installed on your mobile device, select **Next** and follow the on‑screen prompts to add your Amref account to the app.  
   - If you do not have the app installed, a download link will be provided; install the app from that link, then return to this step and select **Next** to complete the setup.

   *(The article notes that you can also enable SMS messages as an alternative verification method; the steps for SMS are not detailed in the retrieved excerpts.)*

4. **Complete the setup**  
   Once the app (or SMS) is configured, you will receive a verification code. Enter that code when prompted and click **Next** to finish the enrollment.

After these steps, your Microsoft 365 sign‑in will require both your password and the second factor you just configured, giving you the extra layer of security described in the article.

**Caveats**  
- The exact wording of buttons and prompts follows the article; if your screen shows slight variations, look for the equivalent “Next” or “Add account” options.  
- If you prefer to use SMS instead of the Authenticator app, select that option when the verification method screen appears and follow the prompts to enter your phone number (the article confirms SMS is supported, though the detailed steps are not provided in the excerpts).

**Sources**  
- Set up your Microsoft 365 sign-in for multi-factor authentication – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=10  
- Student Email; Mcampus Email; Cooporate Email; Official Email (mentions two‑step verification) – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=4

observations.question: How do I log in to the LMS?
observations.answer:
You can log in to the Amref LMS by following these steps:

1. **Open the LMS site** – Type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into your browser’s address bar (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer, or Opera Mini) or search Google for **“lms amref”** and select the result.  
   *Why:* This takes you to the LMS homepage where the login option is located.

2. **Start the login process** – At the top‑right corner of the homepage, click the **“Login/Register”** button.  
   *Why:* Clicking this opens the authentication window for Amref accounts.

3. **Choose Amref email sign‑in** – In the pop‑up window, click the button labelled **“Use your Amref email address to sign in”**.  
   *Why:* This redirects you to the official Amref email login page, which handles your credentials.

4. **Enter your Amref email and password** – On the Amref email login page, type your full Amref email address (format: firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke) and the password that was sent to you, then press **Enter** or click the sign‑in button.  
   *Why:* Successful entry authenticates your account and brings you to the LMS dashboard.

5. **Select your course** – On the dashboard’s left‑hand navigation pane, locate and click **“My courses”**, then choose the course you wish to study (e.g., “induction module”).  
   *Why:* This opens the course page where you can access lectures, assignments, and other materials.

**Note:** If you encounter any issues (e.g., incorrect password or missing email), you will need to reset your Amref email password via the email service or contact the Help Desk for further assistance.

**Source:** How to login to LMS – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=1

observations.question: How do I log into Moodle?
observations.answer:
Logging into Moodle (the Amref LMS) is straightforward once you know where to click and which credentials to use.

**Steps**

1. **Open your browser** (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer or Opera Mini) and type **lms.amref.ac.ke** into the address bar, or search Google for **“lms amref”** and select the result.  
   *Why:* This takes you to the LMS homepage where the login option is located.

2. **Click ‘Login/Register’** in the top‑right corner of the homepage.  
   *Why:* This opens the authentication pop‑up window.

3. **In the pop‑up window, click the button labelled “Use your Amref email address to sign in”.**  
   *Why:* This redirects you to the Amref email login page, which handles the single‑sign‑on for Moodle.

4. **Enter your Amref email address and password** on the Amref email login page, then press **Enter** or click the sign‑in button.  
   *Why:* Supplying correct credentials verifies your identity and logs you into the LMS.

5. **After successful login, you will be taken to the LMS dashboard.**  
   *Why:* The dashboard is your central hub for accessing courses and other resources.

6. **On the left navigation pane, locate and click “My courses”, then choose the course you wish to study (e.g., “induction module”).**  
   *Why:* This opens the specific course page where you can view lectures, assignments, and grades.

**Caveats**  
- Make sure you have the correct Amref email address and password; if you have forgotten your password, contact the Help Desk for assistance.  
- The steps work with the browsers listed above; other browsers may behave differently but are not covered in the knowledge base.

**Sources**  
- How to login to LMS – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=1

observations.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
observations.answer:
I’ll walk you through resetting your student‑portal password so you can log back in.

**Steps**

1. **Open the portal** – Go to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#** and, on the login page, click the **“forgot your password”** link.  
   *Why:* This starts the password‑recovery flow.

2. **Enter your email and CAPTCHA** – Type your **Amref student email address** and the characters shown in the image, then submit.  
   *Why:* The system verifies that you are a legitimate user before sending a verification code.

3. **Provide your phone number and receive the code** – Input the phone number linked to your account; you will receive an SMS with a one‑time code. Enter that code and continue.  
   *Why:* Two‑step verification confirms your identity using something you have (your phone).

4. **Create a new password** – Type a new password that meets all of the following rules, then confirm it:  
   - Minimum **10 characters** long  
   - Contains a mix of **uppercase and lowercase letters**, **numbers**, and **special characters**  
   - Is **not** any of your official names  
   After confirming, finish the process.  
   *Why:* These complexity rules protect your account from easy guessing.

5. **Log in with the new credentials** – Return to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**, sign in with your student email and the new password, and you should now have access to the portal.  

**Caveats**  
- If you do not receive the SMS code, double‑check that the phone number on file is correct; otherwise contact the Help Desk for assistance.  
- The password you choose must satisfy all the complexity requirements listed above; otherwise the system will reject it.

**Sources**  
- Reset your student portal password – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=9  
- Student Portal – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=3

observations.question: My Student Portal login is not working.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re having trouble logging into the Student Portal. The most common fix is to reset your portal password using the self‑service reset feature.

**How to reset your Student Portal password**

1. Open your web browser and go to the Student Portal login page: **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**.  
2. On the login screen, click the **“Forgot your password?”** link.  
3. In the first field, enter your **Amref student email address** (the one ending in @mcampus.amref.ac.ke) and type the characters shown in the CAPTCHA image.  
4. Click **Next** (or press Enter).  
5. On the next screen, enter your **registered phone number** and then click **Send Code**.  
6. Check your phone for the SMS code, enter it into the field provided, and click **Verify**.  
7. You will now be prompted to create a new password. Type your new password in the **Password** field and repeat it in the **Confirm Password** field, then click **Finish** (or **Submit**).  
   - The new password must be **at least 10 characters long**.  
   - It must contain a mix of **uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters** (e.g., !, @, #, $, %).  
   - It **cannot be any of your official names**.  
8. After the reset confirmation appears, return to the Student Portal login page (https://students.amref.ac.ke/#) and log in with your student email address and the new password you just set.

If you follow these steps and still cannot log in, please contact the Amref Help Desk for further assistance.

**Sources**  
- Reset your student portal password – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=9

observations.question: I forgot my password and am locked out.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re locked out — let’s get you back into the student portal.

**How to reset your Amref student portal password**

1. Open your web browser and go to the student portal login page: **https://students.amref.ac.ke/#**.  
2. On the login screen, click the **“forgot your password”** link.  
3. Enter your **Amref student email address** and type the characters shown in the CAPTCHA image, then submit.  
4. Provide your **registered phone number** when prompted; you will receive a one‑time code via SMS.  
5. Enter the SMS code you received and submit it to verify your identity.  
6. Create a **new password** that meets all of the following requirements (type it twice to confirm):  
   - Minimum **10 characters** long.  
   - Contains a mix of **uppercase and lowercase letters**, **numbers**, and **special characters**.  
   - Is **not** any of your official names (first, middle, or last).  
7. After confirming the new password, finish the reset process.  
8. Return to the portal login page and sign in with your **student email** and the **new password** you just set.

**Important:** If the new password does not meet the length, complexity, or name‑restriction rules, the system will reject it and you will need to try again with a compliant password.

*Source: Reset your student portal password – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=9*

observations.question: How do I register for and take a VAS exam?
observations.answer:
I know registering for a VAS exam can feel confusing, but here’s the full process from start to finish.

**Steps**

1. Open **Google Chrome** or **Mozilla Firefox** (Safari is not supported) and go to the VAS portal at **https://vas.amref.ac.ke**.  
2. Log in using your Amref email and password – you can use either of the two login buttons shown on the page (see the screenshot below).  
3. Click the **My courses** button.  
4. From the list, select the exam you want to take (CAT or Final Exams) and click it. This opens the SMOWL registration page.  
5. On the SMOWL registration page, enter your **Full Name** and your **Amref (mCampus) email address** (see the STEP 3 screenshot).  
6. When prompted, allow the SMOWL system to access your webcam so it can capture your image.  
7. Complete the registration **at least 72 hours before the exam start time**.  
8. When the exam time arrives, return to the VAS portal (https://vas.amref.ac.ke), log in again if needed, click **My courses**, and select the same exam.  
9. Click to open **CAT or Final Exams** (as indicated in the VAS interface) to launch the SMOWL‑proctored exam.  
10. Use **Google Chrome** for the best experience while taking the exam.  
11. Complete the exam; SMOWL will monitor your screen and webcam throughout the session.  
12. When you have finished, click the **Submit and finish** button to end the exam and submit your answers.

**Caveats**  
- Register early (≥ 72 h before the exam).  
- Ensure your webcam is enabled and working.  
- Safari cannot be used; stick to Chrome or Firefox.  
- If any step fails, contact the Help Desk for assistance.

**Sources**  
- How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=14)  
- Taking examination With the SMOWL (Screen Monitoring) (https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=15)

observations.question: What is SMOWL proctoring?
observations.answer:
SMOWL is the university’s exam‑proctoring tool that lets lecturers monitor and secure online assessments so that the integrity of the exam is maintained and cheating is prevented. It works together with the VAS‑Exam system (and can be used within the Moodle VLE/LMS) to remotely observe students while they take their exams.

**How SMOWL proctoring works (based on the Help Desk articles)**  

1. **Purpose** – SMOWL is used to monitor and secure online exams, ensuring assessment integrity and preventing cheating【Article 1†L1-L3】.  
2. **Integration** – The tool is employed alongside the VAS‑Exam system and is compatible with the Virtual Learning Environment/Learning Management System (Moodle)【Article 1†L4-L6】【Article 2†L1-L3】.  
3. **User role** – Lecturers set up and supervise exams with SMOWL, while students take the exam while being monitored remotely【Article 3†L1-L3】.  
4. **What happens during an exam** – When a student launches a proctored exam via the VAS‑Exam system, SMOWL runs in the background, capturing webcam, screen, and audio activity to allow remote supervision and to flag any suspicious behaviour【Article 2†L1-L4】.  
5. **Outcome** – After the exam, lecturers can review the recordings/reports generated by SMOWL to confirm that the assessment was conducted fairly【Article 3†L1-L3】.

In short, SMOWL provides the remote‑monitoring layer that, together with VAS‑Exam (and Moodle), enables secure, integrity‑checked online examinations.

**Sources**  
- Exam proctoring software- SMOWL – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=18  
- What Happens During a Proctored Exam with Smowl? – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=21  
- Recorded training session- Lecturer exam proctoring using SMOWL – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=19

observations.question: SMOWL camera is not working during my exam.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re running into trouble with the SMOWL camera during your exam – let’s walk through the exact steps the knowledge base describes for getting the webcam working and confirming that SMOWL is active.

**What you need to do**

1. **Open the exam in VAS‑Exam**  
   - From the VAS portal, select your exam (see the image “Step 1 : Select your exam in VAS”).  
   - Click to open the CAT or Final Exams list (see the image “STEP 2 : Click to open CAT or Final Exams”).

2. **Make sure the SMOWL software is installed and your system meets the requirements**  
   - You should have already downloaded and installed SMOWL (Windows 10/11 or macOS 10.15+ with a stable internet connection) – this is covered in the registration article.

3. **Grant browser permission for the webcam and microphone**  
   - Use Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox (the only browsers noted as supported).  
   - When the pre‑test page loads, allow the browser to access your webcam and microphone.

4. **Enable SMOWL to run**  
   - After granting the browser permissions, click the checkbox that allows SMOWL to run directly at the start of the exam.  
   - Then select the **Open SMOWL** option.

5. **Verify that SMOWL has launched correctly**  
   - You should see the SMOWL block appear, first loading, then display a **navy‑blue computer icon**.  
   - This confirms that SMOWL is active and ready to capture your activity.

6. **Confirm the monitoring state**  
   - Once SMOWL is running, the activity‑in‑progress mode will show a **red “END ACTIVITY” button**.  
   - If the icon is not navy‑blue or the red button does not appear, SMOWL has not started properly.

7. **Proceed with the exam**  
   - Click **“Attempt quiz”** then **“Start attempt.”**  
   - SMOWL will now record your screenshots, web browsing, open programs, etc., as described in the monitoring section.

8. **If the camera still isn’t working**  
   - Return to step 3 and double‑check that the browser’s webcam permission is still allowed (sometimes a page reload resets the permission).  
   - Repeat steps 4‑5 to ensure the navy‑blue icon and red END ACTIVITY button appear.  
   - Only after SMOWL shows the correct icons should you continue to start the attempt.

**Caveats**  
- The knowledge base does not provide alternative troubleshooting steps (e.g., reinstalling drivers, trying a different device, or contacting SMOWL support). If the above verification steps do not resolve the issue, you will need to reach out to the Help Desk for further assistance.  
- Always use Chrome or Firefox; Safari is not supported for SMOWL.

**Sources**  
- Taking examination With the SMOWL (Screen Monitoring) – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=15  
- How to Register and Take Exams with SMOWL Proctoring Software – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=14

observations.question: Where do I sign in to corporate Outlook?
observations.answer:
To sign in to your corporate Outlook (Mcampus/University email) you first log in to the LMS and then open the Student Email link from the Student Services menu.

**Steps**

1. **Open the LMS login page**  
   - In your browser (Chrome, Mozilla, Firefox, Internet Explorer, Opera Mini) go to **lms.amref.ac.ke** or search Google for “lms amref”.  

2. **Start the LMS sign‑in**  
   - At the top‑right of the LMS homepage, click **‘Login/Register’**.  

3. **Use your Amref email to sign in**  
   - In the pop‑up window, click the **“Use your Amref email address to sign in”** button.  

4. **Enter your Amref credentials**  
   - You will be redirected to the AMREF email login page.  
   - Type your Amref email address and password, then sign in.  
   - After successful login you will arrive at the LMS dashboard.  

5. **Navigate to Student Email**  
   - On the LMS dashboard, locate the **Student Services** section (usually in the left‑hand navigation or main menu).  
   - Click **Student Email** under Student Services.  

6. **Complete the corporate Outlook sign‑in**  
   - The Student Email link opens the corporate Outlook (Mcampus) sign‑in page where you will enter your email address in the format **firstname.lastname@mcampus.amref.ac.ke** and complete the two‑step verification (phone‑number code) as described in the email activation guide.  

Once you complete the two‑step verification, you will be logged into your corporate Outlook/University email account.

observations.question: The portal shows an error when I upload a document.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re running into an error while trying to upload a document in the Student Portal. I can walk you through the documented steps for getting into the portal (and resetting your password if needed), but the Knowledge Base does not contain specific guidance for troubleshooting document‑upload errors. For that part you’ll need to contact the Help Desk.

**What the Knowledge Base covers – accessing the portal and resetting your password**

1. Open your browser and go to the Student Portal login page: **https://students.amref.ac.ke/**  
2. If you can’t remember your password, click the **“Forgot your password?”** link on the login screen.  
3. Enter your **Amref student email address** and type the characters shown in the CAPTCHA image.  
4. Provide your **phone number** on the next screen; you will receive a verification code via SMS.  
5. Enter that code, then type a **new password** that meets all of the following rules:  
   - Minimum **10 characters** long  
   - Contains a mix of **uppercase and lowercase letters**, **numbers**, and **special characters**  
   - Is **not** any of your official names  
6. Confirm the new password and finish the reset process.  
7. Return to **https://students.amref.ac.ke/** and log in with your student email and the new password you just set.

**What is not documented**

The Knowledge Base does not include steps for diagnosing or fixing an error that appears when you try to upload a document (e.g., file‑size limits, unsupported formats, permission issues, or specific error messages). Because that troubleshooting information is missing, I recommend reaching out to the Help Desk for assistance with the upload problem.

**Sources**  
- Student Portal – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=3  
- Student portal user guide – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=12  
- Reset your student portal password – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=9

observations.question: Hi, can you help me contact the Amref Help Desk?
observations.answer:
Sure thing — here’s how you can get in touch with the Amref Help Desk using the options documented in the knowledge base.

**How to contact the Amref Help Desk**

1. **Choose your preferred access method**  
   - **Via the LMS** – If you are already logged into the Learning Management System, hover over the **“Student Services”** menu and click the **Help Desk** link.  
   - **Via the website** – Open your browser and go to **http://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke**.  
   - **Via email** – Send a message to **helpdesk@amref.ac.ke** (you will be automatically assigned a ticket).

2. **Open the Help Desk interface**  
   - After using one of the methods above, the AmIU Help Desk page should load.

3. **Submit a ticket**  
   - Click the **“Submit a ticket”** button.  
   - Select the **category** that matches the type of assistance you need.  
   - Fill in the online form with:  
     - Your **name**  
     - Your **email address**  
     - Your **admissions/registration number**  
     - The **priority** of the issue  
     - A clear **subject** line  
     - A detailed **message** describing the assistance you require  
     - Any relevant **files** (attach if needed)  
   - Click the **“Submit Ticket”** button.

4. **Confirmation**  
   - You will receive an email confirming that your request has been submitted.  
   - Any further updates to your ticket will also be sent to you by email.

*Source: How to access the AmIU help desk – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=2*

observations.question: Please help me log in.
observations.answer:
I’m sorry you’re having trouble getting in—let’s walk through the login process for the Amref Learning Management System (LMS) step by step.

1. **Open your web browser and go to lms.amref.ac.ke** (or search Google for “lms amref”).  
   *Why:* This is the LMS homepage where the login option is located【2†L1-L4】.

2. **At the top‑right of the homepage, click the ‘Login/Register’ button.**  
   *Why:* Clicking this opens the sign‑in window【2†L5-L8】.

3. **In the pop‑up window, click the “Use your Amref email address to sign in” button.**  
   *Why:* This redirects you to the Amref email login page so you can use your institutional credentials【2†L9-L12】.

4. **Enter your Amref email address and the password for your Amref account, then submit.**  
   *Why:* Providing correct credentials authenticates you and takes you to the LMS dashboard【2†L13-L16】.

5. **Once on the dashboard, use the left‑hand navigation tool to select “My courses” and choose the course you want to study.**  
   *Why:* This opens your course content so you can begin learning【2†L17-L20】.

*If you don’t remember your password, you can reset it using the student‑portal password‑reset process (minimum 10 characters, mix of upper/lowercase, numbers, special characters, not your official name) before returning to step 4【1†L1-L9】.*

**Sources:**  
- How to login to LMS – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=1  
- Reset your student portal password – https://helpdesk.amref.ac.ke/knowledgebase.php?article=9 (for password reset, if needed)
